candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI also lists lower API prices. An API is the developer-facing connection that lets software send work to a model and pay for the text it processes. Those figures are not a ChatGPT subscription price.
“Sol and Luna are model names, but access and price depend on the service you use. The lower numbers are API prices for developers, not a new ChatGPT subscription bill.”

sourceEvidence.excerpt: GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna are available in ChatGPT Work and Codex starting today for all Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access GPT‑6 Luna in the desktop app. These models are not yet available in Chat.
Prices are per 1 million tokens. GPT‑6 Sol can take on difficult work tasks while giving you more room to iterate with higher usage limits and lower cost.

scopeAndFreshness: The release excerpt states 'Prices are per 1 million tokens', which is usage-metered API billing rather than a subscription figure; P003 attributes the prices to OpenAI, explains what an API is, and draws only the boundary that the figures are not a ChatGPT subscription price. The source implies rather than states the negative, but the inference is faithful and limited.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI says model and reasoning choices depend on a plan and workspace settings.
